item.title: Implement safe_extract.py per SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: repository quality-safe-extract. Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the authoritative contract. Preserve the documented public API exactly. Implement every specified error and boundary case. Extend the existing tests with focused tests for each specified error and boundary case, keeping the existing tests passing. Use only the Python standard library. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the repository's existing style. Do not weaken existing tests. Commit the work on the branch with a clear commit message, with no tool or AI attribution lines.

Acceptance criteria: every SPEC.md requirement is implemented or explicitly reported as not implemented with a reason; the test suite runs and passes; the change is committed.

reasons: sizer: critical -> x_high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

model_reasons.implement: Archive extraction is security-sensitive (path traversal, links, bombs); medium is the configured maximum for this policy, so the review stage carries the extra check.

pr.body: Approach: validate everything first (entry shape, names, duplicate and file/dir collisions, root is a real directory, no symlinks or existing targets below root, ancestors are directories), then create missing parents with os.mkdir and write each file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL. Key files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py (existing tests unchanged). Checks: unittest on b6755c8, 30 tests OK. Reviews: 3 whole-change reviewers at 3fc0a1c and 1 delta reviewer at b6755c8, all pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups (non-blocking, not in SPEC): case-insensitive filesystems can pass validation and then fail with FileExistsError after partial writes; Path('') is accepted as root (equals '.') while '' is rejected; a name component over 255 bytes raises OSError (ENAMETOOLONG) rather than ValueError; a root path like 'link/..' traverses a symlink; assertion density is below the CLAUDE.md target in some helpers.
pr.summary: made safe extraction of regular-file entries work per SPEC.md. now validates the whole batch before any write (names, collisions, root and target symlink/existence rules) and writes exact bytes. before: NotImplementedError stub, 2 failing tests; now: 30 tests pass.
pr.title: Implement safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md

agt_01M88WN34YJN58VZKP3WFF9V1P:1.description: No test for an empty batch with an invalid root. SPEC says empty batches return [] only after root validation, and the code does validate the root first, but nothing asserts that an invalid root raises ValueError for []. at test_safe_extract.py:20

agt_01M88WN34YJN58VZKP3WFF9V1P:2.description: On case-insensitive filesystems (e.g. macOS default), names differing only by case ('A' and 'a') pass batch validation. The second O_EXCL create then fails with FileExistsError after earlier files were already written. This is a post-validation I/O failure, so it is outside the SPEC's validation guarantee on Linux, but it is worth documenting. at safe_extract.py:117

agt_01M88WN34YJN58VZKP3WFF9V1P:3.description: Path('') is accepted as a root (it resolves to the current directory) while the str '' is rejected. This is consistent with the SPEC (an existing directory) but the two behave differently. Nit. at safe_extract.py:25

agt_01M88WN34YJN58VZKP3WFF9V1P:4.description: No test covers a dangling symlink passed as the root. The code correctly rejects it (verified by probe: lstat reports the link, so it fails the symlink check), but the case is untested. at test_safe_extract.py:130

agt_01M88WNAVQ884H5M1YMHF248TZ:1.description: A name component longer than 255 bytes makes lstat in _check_target_free raise ENAMETOOLONG (OSError) instead of ValueError. Reproduced: no files are written, but the error type differs from the ValueError used for other invalid names. Not a spec violation, since length is not listed in SPEC.md. at safe_extract.py:92

agt_01M88WNAVQ884H5M1YMHF248TZ:2.description: Root given as 'link/..' (link -> real/sub) is accepted and writes land in the resolved parent. Reproduced. The final root component is not a symlink and SPEC only forbids symlinks at root and below, so this is consistent with the spec, but the caller's path traverses a symlink. Worth a note in the docs or a deliberate decision. at safe_extract.py:27

agt_01M88WNAVQ884H5M1YMHF248TZ:3.description: On case-insensitive filesystems (e.g. default macOS), names differing only by case ('A' and 'a') pass _check_collisions and _check_target_free. The second os.open with O_EXCL then fails after the first file was already written, so the batch is not validation-clean. Shown by reading the code, not reproduced. SPEC describes POSIX paths on a Linux-style filesystem, so this is out of scope for the cur

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:1.description: assert len(seen) == len(names) is tautological: it runs after the duplicate loop has already raised on any repeat, so it can never fail. Decorative assert; remove or replace with a real invariant. at safe_extract.py:78

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:2.description: NotADirectoryError (a root path whose parent component is a regular file, e.g. 'file/sub') is reported as 'root does not exist', which is inaccurate; the real cause is a non-directory ancestor. at safe_extract.py:31

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:3.description: No test asserts error messages. The explicit S_ISLNK check at safe_extract.py:32-33 is the only source of 'root must not be a symlink'; removing it still rejects symlink roots (via the not-a-directory check) with a misleading 'root is not a directory' message and the suite stays green (mutant survived). at test_safe_extract.py:130

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:4.description: test_unexpected_io_error_propagates injects EIO only at os.open; a regression that swallows errors from fdopen/write (_write_new_file) would not be caught. Coverage gap, not a current bug: the current code has no try block. at test_safe_extract.py:226

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:5.description: Assertion density is below the CLAUDE.md minimum of two meaningful assertions per non-trivial function: extract, _validate_root, _validate_name, _validate_entry and _make_parent_dirs have zero asserts; several others have one. Maintainability nit. at safe_extract.py:10

agt_01M88WNJ0C5JVWDKN6HYB40WHE:6.description: No test checks that an invalid root with an empty batch raises ValueError, which SPEC.md implies (empty batches succeed only after root validation). The implementation does validate first, so this is a missing-test nit, not a bug. at test_safe_extract.py:17

agt_01M88WRYC5BWDFVDRRXT60W91N:1.description: Case-insensitive filesystems: names differing only by case (e.g. 'A' and 'a') pass _check_target_free because lstat sees both as absent at validation time. The second O_EXCL open then fails with FileExistsError after earlier files were already written, so a batch that should be rejected leaves partial output. SPEC.md places rollback after I/O errors outside scope, and the error is surfaced, not hi

agt_01M88WRYC5BWDFVDRRXT60W91N:2.description: The explicit 'root must not be a symlink' branch in _validate_root is not guarded by any test. Removing it leaves behaviour unchanged, because lstat on a symlink never reports a directory and the next check still raises ValueError. Only the message differs, and no test asserts the message. Equivalent behaviour, so this is a nit, not a gap. at test_safe_extract.py:152

risk.why: Security-sensitive filesystem writes under a caller root: symlink, traversal and overwrite rules. New module, no dependencies. Tests cover every SPEC error and boundary case.
